content:
jamie: FYI— we started a staged cordon of some eu-west1 GPU nodes for onboarding at ~15:10 UTC and immediately saw apiserver 503s and watch reconnects spike. Anyone on the control plane?

oncall-bot: INCIDENT open: apiserver-watch-fanout (P1 notify).

ravi: Checking etcd: WAL fsync latency jumped from ~0.8ms -> 48ms right at the cordon start. nvme write queue depth shot up on the provisioner hosts. Logs: `wal sync took 48ms`, `apply timeout`.

claire: We ran parallel model-cache init-containers on drained nodes (downloads + tar extract to local NVMe). I think concurrent warmups saturated NVMe.

nina: Grafana: nvme avg-qdepth 0->160 for ~70s, apiserver watch backlog ~300 -> 2200. Controller-manager lost lease and restarted once.

ops-automation: Quick remediation applied: scaled down warmup jobs by 90%, set provisioner concurrency=1, uncordoned two nodes to spread load. apiserver backlog fell by ~60% in 40s.

jamie: Good. Action items: 1) add disk-heavy init label so provisioner can rate-limit, 2) WAL fsync >10ms alert on etcd, 3) runbook: stagger drains/cordons with jitter, 4) explore shared cache or tmpfs for warmups.

ravi: Also propose lowering kubelet eviction threshold for local-disk pressure on GPU pools so we detect pressure earlier.

claire: I'll file the postmortem and PR for provisioner throttling. Tagging infra for cache options.

jamie: Thanks. Keep this thread updated if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
